## What's new in 0.2.0
This version adds push notifications with [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) beside email, lets the email password stay out of `Email.yaml`, and makes email mode stop with a clear error instead of running with nothing to check. Email only, ntfy only, or both: the console's unattended monitoring now works with any of them. The console's **Search**, the `HtmlFile` output and the GUI work as before. Your settings, search files, campground list, `Camp.History` and theme choice are kept and need no changes; read "Upgrading from 0.1.1" below for the one change that can affect a container.

### Push notifications with ntfy
- ntfy sends push notifications to the ntfy app on your phone or desktop. Create `Ntfy.yaml` in the settings folder with `enabled: true`, the server and a topic, and subscribe to the same topic in the app.
- Choose how Campertron runs in `General.yaml`: the new `outputTo: Ntfy` notifies you with ntfy only and needs no email settings; `outputTo: Email` sends emails and, while `Ntfy.yaml` has `enabled: true`, ntfy notifications too. Without `Ntfy.yaml`, email mode works as before.
- Each check sends one notification for each search with new openings: the title says how many and where ("3 new openings at WATCHMAN CAMPGROUND"), the text lists the dates and sites, and tapping it opens the campground's page on recreation.gov.
- Use the public server `https://ntfy.sh` or your own ntfy server: write the server's address only, without a path or the topic. Use `https`; an `http` address is accepted for a server on a network you trust, and the GUI warns about it.
- **The topic works like a password** on a server without access control, such as `ntfy.sh` without an account: anyone who knows it can read your notifications and send messages to it. Choose a long random topic. Campertron never prints it, and **View Config** and the GUI never show it.
- For a server or topic that needs an access token, Campertron takes it from the file that `tokenFile` in `Ntfy.yaml` names, or else from the environment variable `CAMPERTRON_NTFY_TOKEN`. `Ntfy.yaml` has no setting for the token itself. The token is sent only in the request's `Authorization` header and never printed. A user name and password (ntfy's basic authentication) aren't supported.
- Without a token, Campertron publishes without signing in. That works for a topic anyone may publish to, such as one on `ntfy.sh` without an account, and then the topic's name is its only protection.
- With email and ntfy both on, each check sends to both, and a failure of one doesn't stop the other. An opening is recorded in `Camp.History` once either of them delivered it, so neither sends it again; only openings that neither delivered are reported again at the next start.
- When it starts, Campertron checks `Ntfy.yaml` and the token's source and stops with an error and exit code 1 if ntfy is on but can't be used, or if `outputTo: Ntfy` has no `Ntfy.yaml` with `enabled: true`. It sends no test notification. If a notification can't be sent, Campertron says why and exits with code 1 after the check, as it does when an email fails.
- The GUI's **Settings** offers `Ntfy` as the output and shows whether ntfy is on, never the values of `Ntfy.yaml`; it doesn't edit that file. Write it in a text editor; the README's "Notifications with ntfy" explains each setting.

### The email password can stay out of `Email.yaml`
- Email mode now takes the SMTP password from the first of three places you set up: a file that `smtpPasswordFile` in `Email.yaml` names, the environment variable `CAMPERTRON_EMAIL_PASSWORD`, or `smtpPassword` in `Email.yaml`, as before.
- The password file suits Docker secrets and read-only mounts: write its full path; it holds only the password, with at most one line break at its end, and can be at most 4,096 bytes. Email mode reads it once, when it starts, and never writes, moves or deletes it.
- If the source you set up can't be used (the password file is missing, unreadable, empty or a folder, or the variable is set but empty), email mode doesn't fall back to the next one: it stops right after it starts with an error that says what to fix and exits with code 1, before it searches or sends anything.
- Campertron never prints the password, the password file's path or the variable's value, and removes any password it knows from its error messages.
- It doesn't encrypt the password: anyone who can read the password file, the process's environment or its memory can read it, and so can the computer's administrators. `docker inspect` shows a container's environment variables, so prefer the file.
- The GUI's email settings still show and edit `smtpPassword` only; they say when `Email.yaml` names a password file and warn while `smtpPassword` is also set, because it is then not used.

### Email mode stops when there is nothing to check
- If, when it starts, there is no search file, or no search file is **Enabled (autoRun)** and has a campground, email mode (and the new ntfy mode) writes one error that says what to fix and exits with code 1. Before, it kept running and checked 0 searches every minute.
- Email mode no longer creates the example search `ZionConfig.yaml` when the settings folder has no search file, and creates or changes no file when it stops. The console's **Search** still creates the example the first time you choose it without a search file.
- A container or service set to restart on failure, or always, then starts Campertron again and again with the same error until a search is enabled; with a limited policy, such as Docker's `--restart on-failure:3`, it stays stopped after the last attempt.

### Docker
- The container image works with `outputTo: Ntfy` as well as `outputTo: Email`. The SMTP password and the ntfy token can be mounted as read-only files, for example Docker Compose secrets at `/run/secrets/smtp_password` and `/run/secrets/ntfy_token`, or passed as environment variables.
- The README's "Run it with Docker" shows both, and the repository's `examples/notifications` folder has ready-made settings for email, ntfy and both, and a Docker Compose file.

## Upgrading from 0.1.1
- **Desktop:** extract the new archives and use them instead of your old Campertron folders. Your settings, searches, campground list, `Camp.History` and theme choice are kept and need no changes.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.2.0`, or pull `latest` again, which now points to this version, and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts. `0.2` is new and points to this version too; `0.1` stays on 0.1.1, and `0.1.1` and `0.1.0` don't change.
- **Before you upgrade a container, check that at least one search is enabled and has a campground:** otherwise this version stops right after it starts (see "Email mode stops when there is nothing to check" above).
- **The email password:** nothing to change. `smtpPassword` is still used, unless you add `smtpPasswordFile` or `CAMPERTRON_EMAIL_PASSWORD` is set where email mode runs; then that is used instead.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Going back to 0.1.1
Version 0.1.1 doesn't know what this version added. Before you run it with the same settings folder:
- Remove `smtpPasswordFile` from `Email.yaml` and put the password into `smtpPassword` again: 0.1.1 refuses an `Email.yaml` that has `smtpPasswordFile`, and it doesn't read `CAMPERTRON_EMAIL_PASSWORD`.
- Move `Ntfy.yaml` out of the settings folder and set `outputTo` to `Email`, `Console` or `HtmlFile`: 0.1.1 refuses `outputTo: Ntfy`, its console takes `Ntfy.yaml` for a search file and stops with an error, and its GUI lists it as a search with problems.
- With Docker, use the image tag `0.1.1` (or `0.1`) instead of `latest`.
- `Camp.History` has the same layout in both versions, so neither reports again what the other recorded, including openings that only ntfy delivered. Your search files and the campground list work in both versions unchanged.

## Upgrading from an earlier version
Follow the steps above, and read the upgrade notes of the versions in between: the [0.1.1 notes](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.1.1), and "Upgrading from an earlier version" in the [0.1.0 notes](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.1.0), which lists what changed before 0.1.0 that can affect you, such as how filters with several values match.

## Known limitations
- **ntfy and the new password sources were tested against local stand-ins.** The tests and checks before this release used a stand-in ntfy server, a stand-in SMTP server and a stand-in for recreation.gov on the same computer; no message was sent to `ntfy.sh`, to another ntfy server or to a real email account. ntfy's publishing follows its documentation as of November 22, 2026.
- **Your ntfy topic is stored as plain text in `Ntfy.yaml`.** On a server without access control the topic is all anyone needs to read your notifications. The public `ntfy.sh` keeps messages for some hours and, to reach Android phones, passes them through Google's Firebase service (see ntfy's FAQ).
- **ntfy servers under a path, and basic authentication, aren't supported.** The server must be at the root of its address (`https://ntfy.example.net`, not `https://example.net/ntfy`), and Campertron signs in only with an access token.
- **An `http` ntfy server gets no warning from the console.** Only the GUI warns about it; with `http`, the topic, the token and every message cross the network unencrypted.
- **Your email password can still be stored as plain text** in `Email.yaml`, which gets your system's usual file permissions when Campertron's first start creates it, and the README's Docker steps make the settings folder writable for every user of the computer. A password file or the variable keeps the password out of `Email.yaml`, but Campertron doesn't check who can read the password file or the token file.
- **The GUI doesn't edit `smtpPasswordFile` or `Ntfy.yaml`.** Write them in a text editor; the GUI keeps `smtpPasswordFile` as it is when it saves `Email.yaml`.
- **Email and ntfy mode read their settings once, when they start.** After you change a search file, `Email.yaml`, `Ntfy.yaml`, the password file or the token file, restart Campertron or its container.
- **A refresh needs free disk space.** With recreation.gov's list of November 17, 2026, the folder that holds `CampertronConfig` needed up to about 1.15 GB more than the installed campground list while the refresh ran (measured on Linux), and the database engine also uses some space in your system's temporary folder. Campertron doesn't check the free space before it starts.
- **The refresh and the automatic restart on Windows and macOS.** Both were run in a real window only on Linux. On Windows and macOS the checks before publishing confirm that the GUI finds its own program to restart, but they don't refresh or restart it.
- **The GUI on Windows and macOS.** Before publishing, the GUI is started on Windows and macOS and runs its built-in checks there. Those checks don't cover how the tabs look, keyboard use or screen readers, or whether **System** follows the theme setting of Windows and macOS.
- **Console on Windows and macOS.** The console's layout, colors and menu had a manual visual check on Windows, not a complete test, and haven't been tried on macOS.
- **Checking hundreds of filter values before saving.** Each change re-checks every value you added since the last save, so after checking all 360 campsites of a large campground, each further change takes about a second until you save.
- **The Results tab can take a few minutes when recreation.gov doesn't answer.** A month is asked for up to three times, with a wait of 30 seconds after a failed request, before it is listed as "not checked". **Cancel** ends the wait at once.
- **Searching one campground for the first time in two Campertron programs at once** can make one of the searches stop with an error, because both prepare the campground's site details at the same moment. This has not been seen in testing; if it happens, run the search again.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- **Other notification services**, such as webhooks, Gotify, Apprise, Discord, Telegram or Pushover, aren't supported.
- **The included campground list is recreation.gov's data of November 10, 2026.** Campsites added since then are not reported until you refresh the list, with **Refresh campground data…** in the GUI or **Refresh Ridb Data (slow)** in the console (see "Keep the campground list up to date" in the README).
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). The 32-bit Windows downloads are started on 64-bit Windows before publishing, not on a 32-bit system, and the `linux-arm` downloads are built but not started.
